questions.prompt: What is the required precondition for binary search to work correctly?

options.text: The input must contain no duplicates
The input must be a power of two in length
The input must be stored in a linked list

questions.explanation: Binary search decides which half to discard based on order, so the sequence must be sorted; on unsorted data the result is meaningless.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of binary search on n sorted elements?
questions.explanation: Each step halves the search window, so it finishes in about log₂ n comparisons.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Binary search requires sorted input; linear search does not
Binary search runs in O(log n) time
bisect_left returns the leftmost valid insertion index for a value
Linear search is faster than binary search on large sorted data

questions.explanation: Binary search needs sorted data and is O(log n); bisect_left gives the leftmost insertion point. On large sorted data, binary search's O(log n) beats linear's O(n).

questions.prompt: Each step of binary search discards about one ______ of the remaining elements. (one word)
questions.explanation: Comparing against the middle lets you eliminate half the window every step — the source of the O(log n) bound.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of one binary-search iteration.

items.text: Compare the middle element with the target
Discard the half that cannot contain the target

questions.explanation: Find the middle, compare, throw away the impossible half, and continue on what remains until the target is found or the window is empty.

questions.prompt: Match each search tool with its behaviour.

pairs.right: O(n) scan; works on unsorted data

questions.explanation: Linear search is general but slow; binary search is fast but needs sorting; bisect_left/right give the two insertion points around equal values.
